title: Maximum Frequency Stack
description:
Design a stack-like data structure `FreqStack` that pushes elements to the stack and pops the most frequent element from the stack.

Implement the `FreqStack` class:
- `FreqStack()` constructs an empty frequency stack.
- `void push(int val)` pushes an integer `val` onto the top of the stack.
- `int pop()` removes and returns the most frequent element in the stack. If there is a tie for the most frequent element, the element closest to the stack's top is removed and returned.

Both `push` and `pop` must run in `O(1)` time.
constraints: At most 2 * 10^4 calls will be made to push and pop.
It is guaranteed that there will be at least one element in the stack before calling pop.
hints: Maintain a frequency map freq[val] and a map of stacks group[f] storing all values pushed at frequency level f in push order.
Track maxFreq: pop always removes the top of group[maxFreq], decrements freq[val], and decrements maxFreq whenever group[maxFreq] becomes empty.

examples.explanation: After pushing [5,7,5,7,4,5], 5 has freq 3 so pop returns 5; then 5 and 7 tie at freq 2 with 7 closer to top so pop returns 7; next 5 (freq 2), then 4 (closest to top among freq 1).
When all values are distinct, FreqStack behaves identically to a standard LIFO stack.
After popping down to empty and pushing again, frequencies reset cleanly.
